ontology: User Story -> Narrative + Scenarios (Given/When/Then Steps) -> Behaviors on Interaction Elements over Data

userStory.feature: linked files to announce their type, size, and new-window behaviour, and to be previewable inline
userStory.benefit: I know what a link will do before I activate it, and can read it without losing my place

core.name: A file link lacking format information is repaired
given: a link to "guide.pdf" with the text "Reading room guide"
then: the link's accessible name announces it is a "PDF file"
a link opening in a new window announces "opens in new window"
an inline-view control is offered

guidelines.text: Provide a preview of file contents before download.
guidelines.rationale: The ACC1 rule already injects an inline viewer for supported formats (PDF/DOCX) via the converter; no server change needed.

scenario.name: A supported file can be previewed inline
given: a link to a PDF or DOCX file
then: the file is rendered as accessible HTML in place, without a download

guidelines.text: Offer accessible alternative formats (HTML, EPUB, tagged PDF) whenever possible.
guidelines.rationale: Client-side conversion to accessible HTML/DOCX is algorithmic (the converter does it); EPUB and tagged-PDF generation, or serving them as canonical assets, is an app-layer/authoring task.

guidelines.text: Preserve users' navigation context after viewing or downloading a file.
guidelines.rationale: Rendering inline (rather than navigating away) preserves context; focus is returned on close.

userStory.feature: every meaningful image to have a text alternative, at a level of detail I can choose
userStory.benefit: I can understand what an image conveys

core.name: A content image without a usable alt is flagged, and non- images are found
given: an with no alt, a filename-like alt, an empty alt on a large image, or an SVG/canvas/CSS-background image
then: the element is exposed as an image needing a text alternative (data-mdlaug-needs-alt)
the tool never invents the alt text

guidelines.text: Allow users to choose between brief and detailed image descriptions.
guidelines.rationale: A brief/detailed toggle is algorithmic UI; the two description texts must come from authored alt/longdesc or from a description service prompted at two levels.

guidelines.text: Provide image descriptions at different levels (overview, detailed, scholarly context).
guidelines.rationale: Overview/detailed can be model-drafted, but scholarly/curatorial context is authored knowledge the tool must not fabricate.

guidelines.text: Allow users to request AI-generated supplemental descriptions, clearly identified as AI-generated.
guidelines.rationale: Implemented pattern: with a configured description endpoint the Reading Room fills a description and labels it "unverified". The request UI and labelling are algorithmic; the model is a service.

scenario.name: An AI description is offered and labelled
given: an image needing a description and a configured description service
then: a description is inserted and clearly labelled as auto-generated / unverified

userStory.feature: a graph's data and meaning available as text and as a table
userStory.benefit: I can understand the data without seeing the chart

core.name: A graph is exposed as needing a data description
given: a chart rendered as SVG/canvas/image
then: the graph is given role=img and flagged as needing a data description/table

guidelines.text: Provide downloadable data tables corresponding to every graph.
guidelines.rationale: If the underlying data is present in the DOM (e.g. an SVG's data attributes or an adjacent hidden table) the tool can extract and surface it; a chart rendered as a flat image has no data to extract, so the author/app must supply the table.

guidelines.text: Present textual summaries highlighting trends, comparisons, and outliers.
guidelines.rationale: Requires analysis of the data; a model can draft a summary (service), otherwise authored.

guidelines.text: Allow users to ask natural-language questions about graph content.
guidelines.rationale: A Q&A interface over the data is an application feature, not a DOM remediation.

userStory.feature: a collection exposed as a navigable list with clear hierarchy
userStory.benefit: I can move through items and understand where I am

core.name: A results/collection container is exposed as a list
given: a container of repeated item cards
then: the container gets role=list and each item role=listitem

guidelines.text: Present breadcrumb navigation showing collection hierarchy.
guidelines.rationale: Labelling an existing breadcrumb as a nav landmark is algorithmic (see EXE3); constructing a hierarchy where none exists is app-layer.

guidelines.text: Provide collection statistics (number of items, formats, dates, subjects).
guidelines.rationale: Not reliably derivable from the DOM; comes from the catalogue/backend.

guidelines.text: Allow direct navigation to popular or recently added items.
guidelines.rationale: Requires usage/recency data from the application.

userStory.feature: disclosures to expose and announce their expanded/collapsed state
userStory.benefit: I know whether content is open or closed

core.name: A custom disclosure gets state semantics
given: a header that toggles a panel with no aria-expanded
then: the control gets role=button, aria-expanded, and aria-controls to its panel

guidelines.text: Automatically announce expanded/collapsed status changes.
guidelines.rationale: The tool wires aria-expanded; adding a live-region announcement on toggle is a small proposed extension.

scenario.name: A toggle announces its new state
given: a remediated disclosure
then: the new expanded/collapsed state is announced politely

guidelines.text: Remember users' expansion preferences during the browsing session.
guidelines.rationale: The extension can persist open/closed state in session storage and reapply it — algorithmic but stateful and opt-in.

guidelines.text: Provide "Expand all" and "Collapse all" options.
guidelines.rationale: When a group of disclosures is detected, inject accessible Expand-all/Collapse-all controls.

scenario.name: Group controls are offered
given: two or more sibling disclosures
then: accessible "Expand all" and "Collapse all" buttons are added and operate the group

userStory.feature: search autocomplete exposed as a proper combobox with announced options
userStory.benefit: I can use suggestions with a screen reader

core.name: An autocomplete gets combobox semantics
given: a search box with a custom suggestions panel
then: the input becomes role=combobox with aria-expanded and the list role=listbox / options role=option

guidelines.text: Rank suggestions according to search history and collection popularity.
guidelines.rationale: Ranking is a backend/search concern.

guidelines.text: Provide semantic query suggestions (broader, narrower, related terms).
guidelines.rationale: Requires a thesaurus/knowledge source in the application.

guidelines.text: Allow users to disable or customize auto-suggestions.
guidelines.rationale: The extension can add an accessible control to suppress the suggestions panel; honouring it across a session is stateful.

situations.title: Difficulty understanding a digital library structure

userStory.feature: clear landmarks, one main heading, and a skip link
userStory.benefit: I can orient myself and jump to the content

core.name: Missing structure is added
given: a page with no <main>, no skip link, or a broken heading start
then: a main landmark and a skip-to-content link are ensured and the heading order is sane

guidelines.text: Provide a site overview or orientation page for first-time users.
guidelines.rationale: An authored page/feature.

guidelines.text: Offer an accessible sitemap.
guidelines.rationale: A sitemap can be generated from the site's navigation landmarks (algorithmic first pass); a canonical sitemap is app-layer.

guidelines.text: Maintain consistent page layouts across collections.
guidelines.rationale: A design/authoring policy, not a per-page remediation.

situations.title: Difficulty understanding/navigating the search filtering structure

userStory.feature: the filter panel exposed as a labelled region with grouped controls
userStory.benefit: I can understand and operate the filters

core.name: A facet panel becomes a labelled region
given: a filters sidebar with no region semantics
then: the panel gets role=region with an accessible label and grouped controls

guidelines.text: Display currently applied filters in an easily reviewable summary.
guidelines.rationale: Active filter chips present in the DOM can be collected into a labelled "applied filters" summary region (algorithmic); if the app doesn't render them, it's app-layer.

guidelines.text: Explain how each filter affects search results.
guidelines.rationale: Explanatory content is authored.

guidelines.text: Provide one-click removal of individual filters and "Clear all filters."
guidelines.rationale: Where removable filter chips exist, the tool can ensure each has an accessible remove control and add a "Clear all"; wiring removal to the app is app-layer.

situations.title: Difficulty assessing relevance of a collection or an item

userStory.feature: result titles and snippets that make each item's relevance clear
userStory.benefit: I can decide what to open

core.name: Result items get descriptive link semantics
given: a list of result rows
then: each result's primary link has a meaningful accessible name

guidelines.text: Explain why an item appears in search results.
guidelines.rationale: Match rationale comes from the search engine.

guidelines.text: Highlight matching query terms within snippets.
guidelines.rationale: The tool can read the query (from the URL or the search box) and wrap matches in result snippets with <mark>, exposing them to assistive tech.

scenario.name: Query terms are highlighted in snippets
given: a results page reached with a query "harbor"
then: occurrences of "harbor" in each snippet are marked and announced as highlighted

guidelines.text: Provide AI-generated summaries that explain an item's relevance.
guidelines.rationale: A model can draft a relevance summary (service); the trigger/labelling is algorithmic.

userStory.feature: an accessible, keyboard-operable clear control with feedback
userStory.benefit: I can clear my query and know it worked

core.name: A clear affordance is named and operable
given: a search box with an unlabelled × control
then: the clear control gets a name and is keyboard-operable

guidelines.text: Confirm successful clearing of search terms through accessible feedback.
guidelines.rationale: On clear, announce "search cleared" via a live region.

scenario.name: Clearing is confirmed
given: a remediated clear control
then: the search box is emptied and "search cleared" is announced

guidelines.text: Offer recent searches after clearing the query.
guidelines.rationale: Requires search history from the application.

guidelines.text: Provide an undo option after accidental clearing.
guidelines.rationale: The extension can stash the last query and offer an accessible "undo"; within-page only.

userStory.feature: a way out of any open item or modal by button and Escape, with focus managed
userStory.benefit: I never get trapped

core.name: A modal gets exit semantics
given: an open modal with no aria-modal and no keyboard close
then: the dialog gets role=dialog/aria-modal, a labelled close control, and Escape closes it

guidelines.text: Restore the user's previous reading position automatically.
guidelines.rationale: The extension can remember scroll/focus position on open and restore it on close — within-session, algorithmic.

guidelines.text: Provide multiple exit methods (Back, Close, Escape gesture, voice command).
guidelines.rationale: Escape-to-close and a labelled Close control are added; voice is provided by the assistive technology once the control is named.

guidelines.text: Warn users before leaving when annotations or edits may be lost.
guidelines.rationale: The app must signal that unsaved state exists.

situations.title: Difficulty returning to a previous page

userStory.feature: a clear, labelled way back and a breadcrumb trail
userStory.benefit: I can retrace my steps

core.name: A breadcrumb becomes a labelled landmark
given: a breadcrumb trail with no nav semantics
then: the breadcrumb gets role=navigation with an accessible label "Breadcrumb"

situations.title: Difficulty finding/locating an icon-based search feature

userStory.feature: icon-only controls (like a magnifier) to have names
userStory.benefit: I can find and use them

core.name: An icon-only button is named
given: a button whose only content is an icon glyph
then: the button gets a sensible accessible name (e.g. "Search")

situations.title: Difficulty finding/locating/distinguishing search features at different levels

userStory.feature: each search feature clearly scoped and labelled
userStory.benefit: I know what I'm searching

core.name: Search controls are grouped into labelled regions
given: multiple search inputs at different scopes
then: each search is placed in a labelled search region

guidelines.text: Clearly announce the scope of every search (site, collection, results).
guidelines.rationale: Where scope is inferable from the input's placeholder/label/container, the tool can add a scope to the accessible name; otherwise authored.

guidelines.text: Allow users to switch search scope without losing entered queries.
guidelines.rationale: Query preservation across scope changes is application behaviour.

guidelines.text: Maintain consistent terminology across all search interfaces.
guidelines.rationale: Authoring/content policy.

userStory.feature: help to be findable and usable
userStory.benefit: I can get assistance when stuck

core.name: A help affordance is exposed
given: a help/FAQ control
then: the help control is named and reachable

guidelines.text: Provide contextual help that adapts to the current task.
guidelines.rationale: Task-aware help is an application feature.

guidelines.text: Include short accessible video or audio tutorials.
guidelines.rationale: Authoring the tutorials is manual; captioning/transcribing them is algorithmic via the media rule (MED1) with a transcription service.

guidelines.text: Offer searchable help documentation.
guidelines.rationale: A documentation/search feature.

userStory.feature: stacked windows to trap focus correctly and expose the active layer
userStory.benefit: I don't get lost between layers

core.name: A layered modal is made modal
given: a modal stacked over page content
then: the top layer gets aria-modal and focus semantics so background content is inert to AT

userStory.feature: pagination exposed as a labelled nav landmark with the current page marked
userStory.benefit: I can move between pages

core.name: A pager becomes a labelled landmark
given: a pagination control with no nav semantics
then: the pager gets role=navigation with a label and the active page gets aria-current=page

guidelines.text: Allow users to choose between pagination and continuous scrolling.
guidelines.rationale: A rendering mode of the application.

guidelines.text: Preserve reading position when returning from an item.
guidelines.rationale: Within-session scroll/position restore is algorithmic.

guidelines.text: Announce page transitions and total pages.
guidelines.rationale: On page change, announce "page N of M" via a live region; total is read from the pager.

scenario.name: A page change is announced
given: a remediated pager showing N of M pages
when: the user moves to another page
then: "page N of M" is announced politely

userStory.feature: result updates and structure announced as I move through them
userStory.benefit: I can navigate results confidently

core.name: The results region announces status
given: a results container that updates dynamically
then: a polite live region announces result availability and updates

userStory.feature: an automatic table of contents and heading navigation inside a document
userStory.benefit: I can jump around a long item

core.name: An in-item contents list is generated
given: a long item with a heading outline
when: the page is remediated (or opened in the Reading Room)
then: a Contents list of jump links to the item's headings is provided

guidelines.text: Allow users to bookmark sections within documents.
guidelines.rationale: Within-session anchors/bookmarks are algorithmic; persistent cross-session bookmarks are app-layer.

guidelines.text: Provide automatically generated tables of contents for OCR documents.
guidelines.rationale: TOC-from-headings is algorithmic (implemented); an OCR document first needs OCR (service) to recover headings.

guidelines.text: Support heading navigation even in converted documents.
guidelines.rationale: The converter/Reading Room preserves real headings, so AT heading navigation works on converted content.

situations.title: Difficulty navigating to a search result section

userStory.feature: a shortcut to the results and a focus move when results arrive
userStory.benefit: I can get to results quickly

core.name: A skip-to-results shortcut is added
given: a page with a results section below filters
then: a "Skip to search results" link is provided

guidelines.text: Automatically move focus to search results after search completion (optional).
guidelines.rationale: On search submit, move focus to the results region — offered as an opt-in to avoid surprising focus jumps.

scenario.name: Focus moves to results on search
given: a search that reloads or updates results
the move-focus option enabled
then: focus is placed on the results region and the count is announced

guidelines.text: Announce the location and number of search results.
guidelines.rationale: The results-status live region announces availability/count.

guidelines.text: Provide a "Skip to search results" shortcut.
guidelines.rationale: A skip-to-results link is injected.

situations.title: Difficulty recognizing the availability of search results

userStory.feature: clear, announced status for searching, results, no-results, and errors
userStory.benefit: I know what's happening

core.name: Result availability is announced
given: a results container
then: a polite live region announces when results are available or updated

guidelines.text: Provide progressive feedback during long-running searches.
guidelines.rationale: If a loading state is detectable in the DOM, announce "searching…"; otherwise the app must signal progress.

guidelines.text: Clearly distinguish "no results" from loading or network errors.
guidelines.rationale: The tool can label a detectable empty state as "no results", but distinguishing an error requires the app's state.

guidelines.text: Announce when search results have been updated dynamically.
guidelines.rationale: The live region announces dynamic updates.

situations.title: Difficulty distinguishing collection titles from thumbnails

userStory.feature: titles read before decorative thumbnails, cleanly separated
userStory.benefit: I hear the title, not image noise

core.name: Decorative thumbnails are hidden and titles kept
given: result cards where a thumbnail duplicates the title link
then: purely decorative thumbnails are hidden from AT so the title is what's announced

guidelines.text: Allow users to suppress decorative images entirely.
guidelines.rationale: Decorative/duplicative thumbnails are hidden with aria-hidden; a global suppress toggle is a small proposed extension.

guidelines.text: Present titles before thumbnail descriptions consistently.
guidelines.rationale: Reading order can be corrected with aria-describedby/ordering; visual reordering is riskier and left to the app.

guidelines.text: Separate title and image description with semantic grouping.
guidelines.rationale: Wrapping a title+image pair in a figure/group with a caption is algorithmic where the pairing is unambiguous.

userStory.feature: restricted controls to announce that they're unavailable and why
userStory.benefit: I don't waste effort on features I can't use

core.name: A restricted control is marked
given: a control that is visually gated/locked
then: the control is marked unavailable (aria-disabled) with its reason if detectable

guidelines.text: Explain why a feature is unavailable.
guidelines.rationale: If a reason (e.g. "log in to access") is present nearby, associate it; otherwise the reason must be authored.

guidelines.text: Indicate what actions are needed to gain access.
guidelines.rationale: The required-action text is authored content.

guidelines.text: Avoid presenting inaccessible controls as fully interactive.
guidelines.rationale: Gated controls are marked aria-disabled so AT doesn't present them as operable.

situations.title: Difficulty using screen readers and voice activated commands

userStory.feature: the whole interface to work with my assistive technology and voice control
userStory.benefit: I can use the library the way I use everything else

core.name: Controls carry names/roles that AT and voice control can target
given: interactive controls lacking names/roles
then: controls gain the names and roles that screen readers and voice-control ("click <name>") rely on

guidelines.text: Test compatibility across major assistive technologies (VoiceOver, TalkBack, Narrator, JAWS, NVDA).
guidelines.rationale: Cross-AT verification is a QA process, not a DOM remediation. The tool's automated pass is a first pass; manual screen-reader testing remains necessary.

userStory.feature: every form field to have a programmatic label and clear required/invalid state
userStory.benefit: I can complete forms like sign-in and registration

core.name: Fields are labelled and required state reflected
given: a form with an unlabelled field, a field with only a placeholder, and a required field
then: an adjacent label is associated, or the placeholder is used as a fallback name, and required fields get aria-required
a field with no label and no fallback is flagged for a human-written label

guidelines.text: Identify and describe form errors in text, associated with their field.
guidelines.rationale: Where an error message sits near an invalid field, the tool can wire aria-describedby + aria-invalid; the message wording is authored/app-supplied. (Candidate FORM2.)

guidelines.text: Provide a human-written label when none exists anywhere.
guidelines.rationale: If no label, placeholder, or adjacent text exists, the accessible name must be authored — the tool only flags it.

userStory.feature: video and audio to have captions and a transcript
userStory.benefit: I can access multimedia content

core.name: Uncaptioned media is detected and, with a service, captioned
given: a <video>/<audio> with no captions track, or a YouTube/Vimeo embed
then: the player is named and flagged
with a transcription service, a WebVTT caption track and a visible transcript are added and labelled unverified
third-party embeds are flagged with guidance

guidelines.text: Provide captions/subtitles for video.
guidelines.rationale: Detection, player naming, and building a WebVTT track from returned segments are algorithmic; the transcription itself is a service (or authored captions).

guidelines.text: Provide a transcript for audio and video.
guidelines.rationale: The transcript panel is injected algorithmically; its text comes from a transcription service or is authored.

guidelines.text: Provide audio description for video.
guidelines.rationale: Described-video narration is authored/produced content.
